checks.invariant: stream ticket auth: signature+TTL+slug binding, customer liveness
checks.result: partial: Ticket = signing.dumps({'c':pk,'s':slug}, salt='customer-notifications-stream'), max_age=120s, slug equality enforced, customer re-fetched is_active=True per connect. GAPS: no jti/single-use (replayable within TTL), no tokens_valid_after/logout epoch binding, is_active not re-checked inside _events loop (deactivated customer keeps stream up to 50s), ticket travels in URL query -> access logs/browser history. authenticate_customer does not require email_verified.

checks.invariant: SSE connection concurrency bounded below gunicorn worker capacity
checks.result: fail: Each SSE connection holds one gthread up to STREAM_MAX_SECONDS=50. Capacity = 3 workers x 4 threads = 12 concurrent handlers for the whole API. Only bound = CustomerPublicReadThrottle 'public_read' 1000/hour per IP -> ~864 holds/hour x 50s = ~12 concurrent streams = 100% saturation from ONE IP/account; ticket replayable within 120s TTL; throttle fails open on cache outage.

checks.invariant: SSE event payload isolation, replay bounds, injection safety
checks.result: pass: Last-Event-ID int-parsed, per-poll batch [:50], whitelist serializer payload, JSON-encoded data: lines, bounded 50s generator, clean error handling.

checks.invariant: stream queryset scoped to ticketed customer+store
checks.result: pass with caveat: customer_id filter always applied; foreign pk unreachable without forging signature. CAVEAT: stream-ticket does not validate slug via resolve_store; nonexistent slug -> store_id=None -> store filter dropped -> streams ALL of customer's own notifications (self-scoped, no privilege gain, logic wart).

checks.invariant: error paths bounded, no worker/thread leaks
checks.result: pass: malformed/expired ticket -> clean 401; slug mismatch -> 401; unknown/inactive customer -> 401; generator bounded by monotonic deadline; close_old_connections() per poll.

checks.invariant: SSE chunks reach the wire in real time (no buffering)
checks.result: fail(needs_validation): GZipMiddleware enabled (settings.py:241); Django 5.2.18 compress_sequence reportedly lacks zfile.flush() -> gzip buffers SSE chunks until ~17KB or stream close -> events/heartbeats may not arrive until 50s 'bye'. nginx gzip_types excludes text/event-stream; X-Accel-Buffering:no set. Needs runtime confirmation on installed package.

candidates.title: Single customer account + single IP can saturate all 12 gunicorn gthreads via replayable SSE tickets (full-API DoS)
Stream ticket is a replayable, session-unbound bearer credential in the URL query (120s window)
Django 5.2 GZipMiddleware likely buffers the SSE stream (no per-chunk flush in 5.2.x compress_sequence)

hardening: Add a dedicated throttle scope for the stream endpoint sized for holds plus a per-customer concurrent-stream counter in cache (max 2-3 open streams).
Make stream tickets single-use or near-single-use: embed a jti recorded in cache for the TTL, or shorten TICKET_TTL to ~30-60s.
Bind the ticket to session state (tokens_valid_after/session iat floor) and re-check customer.is_active inside _events every ~15s.
Validate the store slug at ticket mint via resolve_store and treat unknown slug as empty result instead of dropping the filter.
Bypass GZipMiddleware for text/event-stream (set Content-Encoding identity) to preserve heartbeat delivery.
Consider nginx limit_conn for the stream route as a second-layer cap.
Do not log query strings for the stream route (ticket is a bearer credential for up to 120s).
